The only such number is n = 9.

**Setup.** Let p be the smallest prime factor of n. The largest divisor of n other than n is n/p. So the condition is d(n) = n/p. For n = 1 there is no divisor different from n, so n = 1 is excluded and we may assume n > 1.

**Step 1: n is a perfect square.** Since n is odd, every divisor of n is odd. Hence d(n) = n/p is odd. The number d(n) = ∏(aᵢ+1) is odd only if every exponent aᵢ is even. So n is a perfect square, n = m², with m odd.

**Step 2: bounding m.** Pairing each divisor below √n with its complement shows d(n) < 2√n. Thus n/p < 2√n, which gives √n < 2p, i.e. m < 2p.

**Step 3: m = p.** Every prime factor of m is at least p, since p is the smallest prime factor of n = m². If m = p·k with k > 1, then k also has all prime factors at least p, so k ≥ p and m ≥ p² ≥ 2p. This contradicts m < 2p (for any prime p ≥ 3, p² > 2p). So k = 1, m = p, and n = p².

**Step 4: solve for p.** For n = p² we have d(n) = 3 and n/p = p. So p = 3 and n = 9.

**Check.** The divisors of 9 are 1, 3, 9. Then d(9) = 3, which is the largest divisor of 9 other than 9.

ANSWER: 9
